title: 19 — Design a Distributed Message Queue
html:
19 — Design a Distributed Message Queue

The one idea: a modern message queue is a partitioned, replicated, append-only log. Producers append to partitions; consumers track their own offset; ordering holds within a partition; throughput scales by adding partitions; durability comes from replicating each partition with a leader and in-sync followers.

Step 1 — Scope

  • Producers send, consumers receive; messages can be consumed repeatedly (not deleted on read); retained for 2 weeks.
  • Message size in KB range; ordered delivery within a partition.
  • Delivery semantics configurable: at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once.
  • High throughput or low latency, configurable; persistent storage; scalable; available.

Queue vs log:

Traditional queue (RabbitMQ, Service Bus) Event streaming log (Kafka, Event Hubs, Pulsar)
Message removed once acked Retained for a period; replayable
Per-message ack, competing consumers Consumer tracks offset per partition
Great for commands / work distribution Great for events, fan-out to many readers, replay

This design is the log model.

Step 2 — High-level design

Concepts

  • Topic — a named stream. Partition — an ordered shard of a topic. Offset — a message's position in a partition.
  • Broker — a server holding partitions.
  • Consumer group — consumers sharing the work of a topic; each partition is read by one consumer in the group (that's how ordering is preserved and throughput scales).

Step 3 — Deep dive

3.1 Data storage: write-ahead log on disk

  • Each partition = a sequence of segment files; append to the active segment; old segments deleted by retention.
  • Sequential disk I/O is fast (hundreds of MB/s) and the OS page cache does the caching.
  • Zero-copy (sendfile) from page cache to socket for consumers.

3.2 Message format

key, value, topic, partition, offset, timestamp, size, crc — the same format on producer, broker and disk → no re-encoding.

3.3 Batching

Producers batch, brokers write batches, consumers fetch batches. Batch size is the throughput–latency dial.

3.4 Producer flow

Routing layer (in the producer client) picks the partition: hash(key) % partitions (same key → same partition → ordered) or round robin for null keys. Producer buffers and sends batches to the partition leader.

3.5 Consumer flow: pull

Push Pull ✅
Low latency Consumer controls rate; fits batch processing
Can overwhelm slow consumers Empty polls → mitigated with long polling

Rebalancing: when consumers join/leave, the coordinator (a broker) reassigns partitions within the group, triggered by heartbeats.

3.6 Replication and in-sync replicas (ISR)

  • Each partition has a leader and followers on other brokers (replication factor 3).
  • ISR = replicas caught up within a lag threshold.
  • Producer acks setting:
acks Behaviour Durability Latency
0 Don't wait May lose Lowest
1 Leader persisted Lost if leader dies before replication Medium
all All ISR persisted Strongest Highest

3.7 Scalability

  • Producers / consumers: add instances (consumers only up to #partitions per group).
  • Brokers: add brokers, reassign partitions (copy data first, then switch leaders).
  • Partitions: adding partitions changes key → partition mapping → ordering for existing keys breaks; plan partition counts up front.

3.8 Delivery semantics

Semantics How Use
At-most-once Commit offset before processing; acks=0 Metrics where loss is OK
At-least-once Commit offset after processing; acks=all Default — make consumers idempotent
Exactly-once Idempotent producer + transactions (read-process-write atomically) Financial pipelines; costly

3.9 Advanced features

  • Filtering by tags (broker-side, without deserialising the payload).
  • Delayed / scheduled messages — a separate delay store that re-publishes when due.

Step 4 — Wrap-up

Protocol design (AMQP vs custom binary), retry topics and dead-letter topics, retention and compaction (keep the latest value per key), and tiered storage (old segments to object storage).

.NET / Azure mapping

Need Azure service
Replayable event log, partitions, consumer groups Event Hubs (also speaks the Kafka protocol)
Commands, competing consumers, DLQ, sessions (per-key FIFO), duplicate detection, scheduled delivery, transactions Service Bus
Simple cheap queue Storage Queues
Reactive event routing (resource events, webhooks) Event Grid
  • .NET clients: Azure.Messaging.EventHubs (EventProcessorClient stores checkpoints = offsets in Blob Storage), Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus (ServiceBusProcessor, ServiceBusSessionProcessor), Confluent.Kafka.
  • Idempotent consumers: an InboxMessages table keyed by message ID in the same transaction as the side effect.
  • In-process: System.Threading.Channels is the bounded in-memory queue for producer/consumer inside one service.

Review checklist

  • Queue vs log model; chose the log and why.
  • Topic / partition / offset / consumer group.
  • Sequential disk WAL, batching, zero-copy.
  • Leader + ISR replication and the acks trade-off.
  • Delivery semantics tied to offset-commit timing.
  • Ordering is per partition only; partition count is hard to change.
